_about: Per-material design starting points for FDM on a 0.4 mm nozzle. Single source for fx_lib.print_profile() and references/materials.md. Values marked 'default' are conservative starting values chosen by this project, not published figures: calibrate with a fit coupon on the real printer and filament brand. No temperatures or slicer settings live here on purpose: keep those in the slicer profile.

_sources.fits: Markforged design tips: press 0.00-0.05, close 0.05-0.10, free 0.10-0.20 mm, all DIAMETRAL (total across both sides), for their printers
_sources.overhang: All3DP: under 45 to 60 degrees from vertical, or protruding under 5 mm into air
_sources.wall: Objective3D: about 1 to 2 mm minimum, thicker for load
_sources.process: HazAT codex-fusion-360: keep fit allowance separate from material compensation, no global shrink factor, test with a coupon

fit_base_diametral_mm._note: Diametral clearance added between mating parts on a hobby 0.4 mm FDM printer before the material offset. Markforged published values are tighter because their machines are tighter.

notes: Softens in a hot car or near heat, so keep it away from sun-exposed or heated uses.
Cools fast, so it tolerates the steepest overhangs and longest bridges of the common filaments.
Brittle: use fillets and thicker snap arms.
Strings and sags more than PLA on bridges and overhangs.
Sticks hard to smooth plates, so avoid large flat bed-contact faces on mating surfaces.
Good for keychains, clips and snap fits.
Warps: avoid long flat bed faces and sharp corners, fillet or chamfer edges normal to the bed.
Print enclosed. Ventilate: it emits fumes.
All3DP: for a wider part, PETG or nylon may print more reliably.
Like ABS but UV stable: the choice for outdoor and car-exterior parts.
Warps without an enclosure. The H2C heated chamber helps, but still round corners and avoid long flat bed faces.
Ventilate: it emits fumes.
Flexible: design for compression, not rigid fits. Wall thickness sets the stiffness.
Avoid thin tall features and long bridges.
Hole and slot clearances close up when the part flexes: test by hand.
Nylon absorbs water: print from dry filament and expect small size changes in humid use.
Warps strongly: round corners, avoid big flat faces, print enclosed.
High heat resistance and strength, very high warp risk.
Needs a hardened or high-temperature capable hotend: the H2C hotend reaches 350 C.
Carbon-filled: stiff, low warp and shrink, matte finish, abrasive: needs a hardened nozzle.
Fibres align with the toolpath, so strength is highest in the XY plane: put the main load across XY (Markforged makes the same point for composites).
Do not use for snap fits or thin hooks.

PETG-CF.snap_fit: fair: stiffer and less forgiving than PETG
notes: Carbon-filled PETG: stiffer, less stringing, abrasive: needs a hardened nozzle.
Strongest in the XY plane.
Carbon-filled nylon: stiff, strong, low warp compared with plain nylon, abrasive.
Dry the filament, print enclosed, strongest in the XY plane.
